stem: The bar graph shows the number of medals of each type won by a school's track team at a regional meet. If one of the team's medals is selected at random, what is the probability that it is a bronze medal?

figure.title: Medals won by the track team

solution: Read the bar heights: 5 gold, 9 silver and 16 bronze medals, so the team won \(5 + 9 + 16 = 30\) medals in all.
The probability of selecting a bronze medal is \(\frac{16}{30} = \frac{8}{15}\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This treats the three types of medal as equally likely, but there are different numbers of each type.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is \(\frac{14}{30}\), the probability that the medal is NOT bronze.
explanation.C: Correct. There are 16 bronze medals out of \(5 + 9 + 16 = 30\) medals, so the probability is \(\frac{16}{30} = \frac{8}{15}\).
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is \(\frac{5}{30}\), the probability of selecting a gold medal; the bronze bar is the tallest one.

verify:
pts = dict(figure['series'][0]['points'])
tot = sum(pts.values())
assert tot == 30
p = Rational(pts['Bronze'], tot)
assert p == Rational(8, 15)
assert value(choices[answer]) == p
assert all(value(choices[k]) != p for k in choices if k != answer)
